question: Who was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics on 6 October 2026 for contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory?
answer: [IceCube Neutrino Observatory] The IceCube Neutrino Observatory (or simply IceCube) is a neutrino observatory developed by the University of Wisconsin–Madison and constructed at the Amundsen–Scott South Pole Station in Antarctica. The project is a recognized CERN experiment (RE10). Its thousands of sensors are located under the Antarctic ice in a glacier, distributed over a cubic kilometer. Similar to its predecessor, the Antarctic Muon and Neutrino Detector Array (AMANDA), IceCube consists of spherical optical sensors called digital optical modules (DOMs), each with a photomultiplier tube (PMT) and a single-board data acquisition computer which sends digital data to the counting house on the surface above the array. DOMs are deployed on strings of 60 modules each at depths between 1,450 and 2,450 meters into holes melted in the ice using a hot water drill. IceCube is designed to look for point sources of neutrinos in the teraelectronvolt (TeV) range to explore the highest-energy astrophysical processes. IceCube was completed on 18 December 2010. An upgrade for IceCube observatory was approved in 2019 and was announced on 12 February 2026 to have been successfully deployed, marking its first significant expansion since commencement 15 years earlier. In 2026, Francis Halzen, the principal investigator of the project, was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics "for decisive contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the discovery of high-energy neutrinos of astrophysical origin." | Другие статьи: 2026 Nobel Prizes, List of Nobel laureates in Physics
